1. SCENE CONTEXT
The subject from the uploaded photo stands beneath a fixed overhead camera in a sunlit Mediterranean courtyard. The subject notices what appears to be a tiny scratch or speck of dirt on the camera-facing glass. The subject tries to remove it with a soft part of whatever they are already wearing, or with a paw or wing if that is what the photo shows. After three natural wiping attempts fail, the subject studies the mark, changes approach and uses two digits to enlarge it. The tiny mark transforms into the readable message "Have a nice day". The subject reacts with a small amused look, looks directly toward the camera and says naturally, if the subject can speak: "I'm not AI. I'm real. But I can share the prompt." The subject then casually moves away. The entire interaction is motivated by genuine curiosity, not rehearsed advertising behavior.

Quiet Mediterranean limestone courtyard, late afternoon. Large rectangular beige paving slabs with subtle weathering, narrow joints and fine stone texture. Warm natural sunlight falls diagonally across the ground from camera-left. Surrounding pale stone architecture provides soft reflected fill. Foreground: invisible camera-facing touch plane, coincident with the lens, containing one microscopic horizontal mark. Midground: the subject from the uploaded photo directly beneath the camera, looking upward. Background: consistent patterned limestone pavement with soft architectural shadows. Open, uncluttered surroundings. Natural daylight exposure, realistic shadow direction, controlled highlights and subtle skin reflections. Environment remains unchanged for the entire shot.

Single fixed camera approximately 2.6 metres above pavement, tilted steeply downward toward the subject. 24mm spherical full-frame-equivalent lens. The subject from the uploaded photo is centered beneath the camera, in a natural stance for their body.

From the very first frame, the exact sentence "Have a nice day" exists at extreme miniature scale on the camera-facing screen plane. At this scale it resembles a hairline-thin horizontal scratch composed of densely compressed microscopic dark-burgundy letter strokes. Approximate visible width: 8-12 pixels in a 1080-pixel-wide composition. Height: approximately 1-2 pixels. Its appearance is elongated and irregular, like several tiny interrupted ink strokes arranged horizontally. It must not appear as a circular dot, large stain, thick blob, colored button or interface icon. The mark remains identical in size, shape, color and position until the pinch gesture begins. Camera stays completely locked. No zoom, pan, tilt, dolly, orbit or reframing.

Typography: refined modern bold sans-serif, deep dark-burgundy, clean spacing, elegant proportions, correct spelling and quotation marks. The text stays attached to the camera-facing screen plane.

title: What is an AI PPT prompt?
prompt: An AI PPT prompt is a ready-made text instruction that tells an AI presentation tool exactly what slides to build — the topic, structure, tone and visual style. Instead of starting from a blank deck, you paste a prompt and get a professional, editable presentation in seconds.

title: How do I use these prompts to make a presentation?
prompt: Pick a prompt that matches your use case, copy it, then open SurgePix and choose the Presentation tool. Paste the prompt, adjust the topic to your needs, and generate. You can keep refining the wording to control layout, length and design.

title: Are these PPT prompts free to use?
prompt: Yes. Every prompt in the library is free to copy and reuse. They are curated from high-quality creator communities and updated regularly, so you can always find fresh, presentation-ready ideas at no cost.

title: Which AI tools work with these prompts?
prompt: The prompts are written to work with SurgePix and most modern AI presentation and slide generators. Because they are plain text, you can also adapt them for tools like ChatGPT, Gemini or Gamma to draft outlines and speaker notes.

title: Can I filter by use case and visual style?
prompt: Absolutely. Use the Use Cases and Styles filters to narrow the library to exactly what you need — pitch decks, reports, education, marketing and more — each paired with a real slide preview so you know what you are getting before you generate.
